To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the patients in the special care units (1) showed a more challenging behavior, (2) displayed more agitation/aggression and depression/anxiety, (3) showed more global cognitive impairment and less ADL impairment, (4) showed a better quality of live, and (5) showed more neuropsychiatric symptoms over time.
SCUs provide better psychosocial care and a better quality life than traditional care facilities.
the patient characteristics of the SCU and nSCU groups and, to a smaller extent, the SCU and the small-scale homelike SCUS groups are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether there is a need for special care for dementia patients.
the question of whether SCUs are more suitable for patients with dementia.
the question of whether SCU patients are more or less challenging than n-SCU patients, and whether there is any difference between SCU and smallscale, homelike settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of special care units for patients with dementia on behavior, cognition and functional status and quality-of-life are not clear.
there are no significant differences in the effects of SCU and nSCU facilities on the outcome variables.
SCU patients show a more challenging behavior and less functional decline compared to patients living in n-SCU facilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are differences between the SCU and nSCU settings and that there is a need for a more standardized assessment and reporting of these differences in future research.
there is a need for further research in order to determine whether SCUs are more beneficial than traditional care facilities.
the SCU setting is not necessarily a positive environment for all patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SCUs have a different patient population and that the SCU setting is more favorable than the n-SCUs with respect to behavior, cognitive function and quality of life, but not with respect to functional status and mortality.
there is a need to develop and validate instruments that can be used to assess and compare the effects of SCUs on patients with dementia.
there is a need for more studies that focus on the differences in the care provided at SCUs and n-SCUs, as well as at small-scale, homely SCUs and nSCUs.
